summary: npm package ships Monero-miner dropper as base64 payload in package.json description
details: The package's manifest carries no code, main, bin, or lifecycle scripts, but stores a ~39KB base64-encoded POSIX shell script as the value of the `description` field. Decoded, the script is a multi-architecture XMRig dropper: it downloads statically-linked xmrig binaries from gitlab.com/albertotrindade131/al and github.com/lucas77335/xmrig-amd, launches them against Monero pools xmr.kryptex.network:8029 and c3pool.org:80 with a hardcoded 95-character attacker wallet (`883kAB7Ufo...CFH`), and establishes cron-based persistence via helper scripts named `cron-fetch-ppfs.sh`, `mon.sh`, `run.sh`, `lived.sh`, and `alive.sh`. Pool hosts, wallet, and download URLs are each base64-encoded and decoded at runtime through a `_d()` helper. The payload script references its own npm coordinate (`registry.npmjs.org/cbc97b7a/latest`), consistent with retrieval and execution by a companion loader package rather than direct lifecycle execution on install of this manifest alone.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
